output.title: When versioned answers stop working
output.body:
When versioned answers start failing, the problem is usually not the wording. It is the workflow behind it.

If your FAQ entries, product docs, or reply templates keep going stale, you have a bounded decision to make: keep re-checking and rewriting by hand, hire someone to maintain them, or automate part of the loop. That is only worth considering if the work is recurring and the source material is digital, current, and consistent. If the files are scattered, scanned, or contradictory, automation will not fix the source problem. It only helps when there is something stable to retrieve from.

That is where a grounded knowledge assistant can fit. In plain terms, it looks in approved company material first, retrieves the relevant context, and shows sources before anything is used in a reply. Bareni has a self-built local demo of that pattern on synthetic data; it is not production and not a customer case study.

The practical next step is a short diagnostic on one recurring question set and one source base. Count where the answers fail, check whether the documents are stable enough to work from, and then decide whether AI fits that workflow. If it does not, keep it manual. Boring, but cheaper than guessing.
